issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement (UML and textual description) declares messageOnMilk() with return type boolean (problem_statement.md lines 51-53 and line 93), but the solution repository defines the interface and implementations returning String. In the solution, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared as returning String (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5) and Seal/Goat implement messageOnMilk() to return descriptive Strings (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19 and src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 15). This mismatch between the specified boolean return and the solution's String return will confuse students about the correct interface signature and expected behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across specification, template, and solution. Two viable fixes: (A) If the intended behavior is to return success/failure, change the solution: update src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java to declare boolean messageOnMilk(); and update Seal and Goat implementations to return boolean (e.g., true for successful milking); adjust any callers/tests to handle booleans. (B) If descriptive milking messages were intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnMilk() returns String and document the expected message format, and update the textual description (remove the 'true/false' wording). Apply the option that aligns with tests and teaching intent; ensure template/starter code and tests are updated to match the chosen signature.
